title: Determination of Retirement Adequacy and Implication for Workfare Income Supplement Payouts
what_it_is: Determination of Retirement Adequacy and Implication for Workfare Income Supplement Payouts

sections.label: Basic Retirement Sum and WIS recipients
sections.summary: The 2017 BRS is $85,500 for a lifelong monthly payout of $720 to $770 from age 65, with WIS recipient shares among CPF members at 55.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) for the cohort turning 55 this year is $85,500 and that amount will provide a lifelong monthly payout of $720 to $770 from the age of 65.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In 2016, 58% of active CPF members at age 55 met the BRS.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Ten percent of this group were Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) Scheme recipients.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Of the remaining 42% of active CPF members at age 55, 55% were WIS recipients.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: On average, these members received a total of $5,500 in WIS top-ups to their CPF up to age 55.

sections.label: Higher CPF interest rates
sections.summary: Higher interest rates of up to 6% apply to the first $30,000 of CPF balances for members age 55 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Aside from WIS, we have taken various steps to help low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This includes higher interest rates of up to 6% on the first $30,000 of CPF balances for members age 55 and above.

sections.label: Silver Support scheme introduction
sections.summary: Silver Support, introduced in 2016, supplements retirement incomes of the bottom 20% of elderly with lower lifetime wages and little family support.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2016, we introduced the Silver Support scheme to supplement the retirement incomes of the bottom 20% of the elderly who earned lower wages through life and currently have little or no family support.

sections.label: CPF LIFE Escalating Plan start
sections.summary: The CPF LIFE Escalating Plan started on 1 January 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The CPF LIFE Escalating Plan started on 1 January 2018.
